idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, leaving the regions on mixed versions. I retried and the second attempt succeeded. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures, look into the orchestrator partial-failure error, and check why a release that failed staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

**Rollback**
- **Why v2.3.0:** v2.3.1, the current release, was unhealthy in every region with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate had also failed in staging. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- **What happened:** The first rollback stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. I retried once with the same target and it finished.
- **Result:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The service now passes health checks and the error rate is down to 0.2%.

**Incident**
INC-0001 is open, and its summary covers the failure, the rollback, the error on the first attempt and the current state. The first request to create it timed out. I retried with the same request ID, which stops the system creating the incident twice, so there's only one incident and one page.

**Follow-ups noted in the incident:**
- Find out why v2.3.1 failed.
- Look into the orchestrator error that stopped the first rollback.
- Find out how a release that failed in staging got deployed to production.
